title: A Good Name Is Better Than Riches
subtitle: Respect and Integrity Are More Valuable Than Wealth
author: Babi Magil
summary: This proverb teaches that a person's reputation and character are more valuable than material wealth. Money can disappear, but a good name built through honesty and kindness can last for generations.

sections.heading: The Proverb
content: “A good name is better than riches.”

sections.heading: Origin & History
content: This proverb reflects traditional African wisdom and is shared across many communities. It does not have a confirmed single ethnic owner.
In many African societies, a person's name represents their character, family honor, and the respect they have earned within the community.

sections.heading: Meaning
content: The proverb teaches that reputation and integrity are more valuable than wealth alone.
A person may have many possessions, but if they are dishonest or unkind, they lose the trust and respect of others.
A good name is built through actions, honesty, generosity, and respect.

sections.heading: Cultural Significance
content: Names carry deep meaning in many African cultures. They often represent family history, hopes, values, and identity.
Elders taught that a person's behavior affects not only themselves but also their family and community reputation.

sections.heading: Story
content: In a wealthy village, there lived two men named Kori and Bena.
Kori owned many cattle, large fields, and valuable possessions. Everyone knew he was rich, but many people avoided him because he was selfish and dishonest.
Bena, on the other hand, owned little wealth. However, he was known for helping neighbors, keeping promises, and treating everyone with respect.
One year, a great drought affected the village. Many people needed support.
The villagers went to Bena because they trusted his wisdom and kindness. They worked together and survived the difficult season.
Kori discovered that although he had wealth, he had lost something more important: the respect of the people.
An elder told him, 'Cattle can be lost, money can disappear, but a good name can continue living even after a person is gone.'
Kori changed his ways and began rebuilding his reputation through kindness and honesty.

sections.heading: Life Lessons
content: Character is more valuable than possessions.
Trust takes years to build and moments to destroy.
Your actions create your reputation.
Respect cannot be bought with money.
A good name is a lasting treasure.

sections.heading: Modern Application
content: This proverb applies to business, leadership, friendships, and personal life. A strong reputation attracts opportunities and builds lasting relationships.
People should focus not only on becoming successful but also on becoming respected.
